prompt: Stage 2-1, the first augment round, and the first time the planning timer is long enough to scout all seven boards. You have a pair of a 1-cost carry and two AD components. What is the single most useful thing to look for on each board during this scout?

options.label: Which components each player holds and which 1-cost units they are pairing: it tells you who will contest your carry
Which board is strongest, so you know who will beat you
Where each player puts their carry, to prepare positioning

explanation:
At 2-1 nobody has a board worth fearing and positioning against 1-cost units is irrelevant. The one thing that changes a decision this early is contest, and contest shows in two places: the components a player holds (AD components on a bench mean an AD carry line) and the 1-cost pairs they are keeping. Two players with your carry paired and AD items is the information that turns your reroll plan into a flex opener before you spend a gold on it.

The strongest board matters from 3-2 onward, when HP starts to move. Carry positions matter from 4-1, when carries exist. Scouting is a budget; at 2-1 you spend all of it on the contest read.
principle: At 2-1 scout for contest: components held and 1-cost pairs, not board strength.
commonMistake: Looking at everyone's board strength at 2-1 and concluding nothing, because there is nothing to conclude from it yet.
